A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ANIE research. Their main text, equations, figures, table and appendices are readable and support comparison, including v1 Appendices A–F and v3 Appendices A–G.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic intensity-estimation experiments, UCI anomaly-detection results, runtime measurements and resolution-sensitivity experiments in Figures 2, 3, 5 and 6.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds TensorSplat comparison results and London bike-sharing and Enron analyses in Figure 3 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the basis decomposition, truncated-SVD subspace estimation, affinity coefficients and statistical thresholding. Section 5.2 changes the derived UCI anomaly score from a sum of absolute affinity coefficients to their Frobenius norm, modifying the detection output.

E1.justification: V3 retains ER-blocks, SBM and UCI coverage and adds London bike-sharing and Enron employee-email networks in Appendix G. This substantially broadens the real-world domains and populations beyond v1's university messaging example.

E2.justification: TensorSplat is added alongside LAD in the UCI comparison, with an actual reported trajectory in Figure 3. The synthetic IPP-Hist and IPP-KDE comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The UCI scoring rule changes to a Frobenius norm. V3 also introduces consecutive PARAFAC-factor distances for the TensorSplat comparison and scaleogram and embedding analyses for the new case studies. Existing synthetic network-size ranges, MISE evaluation and Table 1 hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds substantial diagnostic case studies: raw versus reconstructed scaleograms distinguish edge fluctuations from latent structural changes, London embeddings are examined by borough, and Enron patterns are compared with an event timeline. The runtime and resolution-sensitivity analyses already existed in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report synthetic MISE means and standard errors over ten runs. V3 introduces no new seed reporting, repeated-run policy, confidence intervals or uncertainty-estimation procedure for the added real-world results.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds TensorSplat results and replaces ANIE trajectories under the revised score definition, while retaining the spring-term and fall-term findings. Figures 7–8 add London embedding and scaleogram findings and Enron temporal patterns. Synthetic estimation, runtime and sensitivity results remain unchanged; the revised UCI curves do not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.2 and Appendix C substantively reformulate the CLT conditions: v1's shrinking intensity bounds and O(1/N) squared loadings become mu_N-dependent loadings with the joint condition mu_N^3(beta_N/alpha_N)^(3/2)/N tending to zero. Appendix B also changes the concentration argument's entry bound from O(sqrt(N rho_N)) to O(log N). Theorem 4.1's full-rank and incoherence assumptions were already present in v1's appendix; their relocation is not new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statement retain the same central claims: adaptive multiresolution network intensity estimation through low-rank structure and statistical thresholding, supported by consistency and asymptotic-normality results. The additional experiments do not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds a PARAFAC-based explanation for TensorSplat's association with message volume and interprets London borough patterns and Enron's later fluctuations. Figure 3 no longer asserts fewer false positives than LAD. Existing variance-estimation and computational-scaling limitations remain.

D1.justification: The implementation link changes from an anonymous repository to the named ANIE GitHub repository. Appendix G supplies the London data source, May 1–8, 2017 window, 219,515 interactions, 780 stations and trip-to-event construction. Hardware, core pseudocode, synthetic hyperparameters and LAD defaults were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for TensorSplat, Transport for London's data and Passino and colleagues' bike-sharing point-process work. It also explicitly connects subspace estimation to UASE and distinguishes ANIE's offline setting from the already-cited online CUSUM approach. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized rewriting clarifies Haar indexing, affinity coefficients and experimental descriptions; Section 5.2 gains explicit dataset, setting and results paragraphs. Assumptions move into the main theorem statements, and acknowledgments are added. The main section sequence and much of the prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 adopts conference formatting with revised typography, margins, author block and headers. Figure 3 is substantially redesigned with stacked per-scale ANIE panels and a TensorSplat panel. New Figures 7–8 add scaleograms, a London embedding and an Enron event table; existing synthetic and appendix plots are retained and reflowed.

improvement.justification: V3 provides broader practical evidence through TensorSplat and two additional real-world case studies, makes theorem conditions more visible and improves the readability of Figure 3. Removing its unquantified fewer-false-positives assertion also improves restraint. These gains are limited by the qualitative nature and incomplete experimental specification of Appendix G; the central quantitative benchmarks and uncertainty evidence remain unchanged.
